client_frame: Split tape into weekend: **SPX hit a NEW RECORD (7,489.72, intraday 7,512) despite AAPL cratering -9.2%** — the widest single-day AAPL vs SPX divergence in a year. AMZN filled the leadership gap (+13.6% cash) as AWS $42.2B posted its fastest growth in 18 quarters (+36.7%). Energy earned its month: **XOM+CVX combined Q2 profits >$26B, +300% YoY** on Iran-spike windfall (CVX refining +500%). **John Ternus takes over as AAPL CEO Sept 1** — succession was announced back in April, Thursday's print was Cook's ceremonial last call. **ECI Q2 came in HOT** (+0.9% QoQ vs +0.8% cons, +3.4% YoY) — the wage-pressure signal Warsh warned about, and FedWatch Sept +25bp odds jumped to 71%. **10Y yield +8bp to 4.745%; 30Y crossed 5.00% first time since 2007**. VIX collapsed sub-16 despite: (1) US/Israel actively weighing strikes on Iranian ENERGY infrastructure (Kharg Island oil terminals per Reuters/WSJ) — a sharp escalation from IRGC-only targets, and (2) Hormuz still ~2 tankers/day (CENTCOM disputed Iran's closure claim but traffic tells the story). **Weekend risk is asymmetric**: (a) If US/Israel strike Iranian energy, oil gaps $10+ Monday open + risk-off. (b) If quiet, momentum tape continues but faces NFP Fri Aug 7 (cons +87-91k) + Sept 15-16 FOMC. **Client message**: buying weekend hedges at VIX 15.99 is cheap insurance against a 25% up-move if oil spikes on strikes; the record SPX print is coming into month-end + reduced-liquidity August with 30Y at 5%.
